finding.expected: Establish one authoritative Human-facing synchronization/admission boundary for a PRIMARY launch. A launch that begins behind upstream may perform at most one native fast-forward-only integration attempt; no second sync/integration window may occur between successful preflight and admission. If that synchronization changes kernel source or canonical TASK state, control must transfer exactly once to synchronized code before TASK loading/admission. Add deterministic regressions through the actual Human-facing main() path for an upstream race between preflight and admission and for TASK-only upstream advancement. Preserve no-retry/no-fallback, correction-flow isolation, exactly-one Executor invocation, and existing Runtime verification semantics.
finding.issue: TASK-062 revision 2 requires one Human-facing pre-admission synchronization boundary with exactly one native fast-forward-only integration attempt when local main is behind. The candidate performs synchronization in main() through _preflight_primary_sync(), then _run_task_impl() independently calls _synchronize_primary_branch() again under a second lock. If upstream advances in the interval, the same Human-facing launch can perform a second integration attempt before admission. The current regression proving one merge calls run_task() directly and therefore does not exercise the actual main()->preflight->run_task path. The same split boundary also leaves TASK-only synchronization changes outside the restart predicate: _is_kernel_source() recognizes pyproject.toml/src changes but not .ai/tasks state, so a TASK-only advance does not establish the revision-2 requirement that control transfer occur exactly once before TASK load and admission when TASK state changes.
